nodes.question: What do co-benefits imply according to the content?
nodes.answer: Co-benefits occur when solutions proposed by one sector achieve positive effects for other sectors.
nodes.paragraph: integrative potential . Integrative potential is de ned here as the opportunity to implement solutions that contribute to solving multiple societal chal-lenges at the same time [as they] may provide co-bene its or synergies (Warbroek et al. 2023 p. 97). Co-bene its occur when solutions proposed by actors of one sector alsoachieve positive effects for other sectors (Duguma et al. 2014 ; Kongsager 2018 ). Synergy, on the contrary, requires actors to focus on the bigger picture and address multiplechallenges from the beginning. Compared to approaches that focus only on one challenge, an integrative approach that addresses multiple challenges is more likely to providesynergetic bene its (Shari 2021 ). Yet, in some contexts, the sectoral approach might prove to work better. For instance, when the causes and effects of a problem are bound by onesector only (Bryson et al. 2006 ; De Lo and Patterson 2017 ). Even so, consideration of integrative potential is often still highly desirable, especially in more complexcontexts where multiple challenges are at stake, such as, climate adaptation and sustainable development goals *Joanne Vinke-de Kruijf joanne.vinke@utwente.nl 1University of Twente, Enschede, Netherlands 1234567890();, 1234567890();, (Cuevas 2016 ), climate adaptation and mitigation (Matocha et al.
